Solver implementation checklist¶

This checklist distinguishes implemented capabilities with verification evidence from outstanding implementation and validation work. A checked capability has passed its stated tests; it is not a guarantee for every application.

Implemented capabilities¶

  • [x] 1. Verification and diagnostics

    • [x] Track mass, species inventory, momentum, angular momentum, kinetic energy, material work/dissipation, external work, and constraint impulses.

    • [x] Report support loss, invalid deformation, density/volume ranges, and timestep restrictions; do not silently hide invalid state.

    • [x] Analytical/convergence checks and reproducible benchmark report.

  • [x] 2. Consistent deformation, volume, density, and stress

    • [x] Store reference volume, deformation gradient, determinant, and histories; update volume/density from deformation with constant particle mass.

    • [x] Objective stress integration and physical fluid bulk/shear conventions; explicit compatibility configuration.

    • [x] Rotation, affine compression, stress/work, inlet/outlet, and species tests.

  • [x] 3. Interchangeable interpolation and quadratic B-splines

    • [x] One stencil interface for weights, gradients, nodes, and physical offsets.

    • [x] Linear and quadratic implementations, including physical boundaries and periodic seams; no clipping/renormalisation that breaks completeness.

    • [x] Generalise every transfer, including segregation, to stencil size.

    • [x] Partition, affine reproduction, gradients, cell crossing, and convergence.

  • [x] 4. APIC

    • [x] Matched particle/grid affine transfers with explicit affine momentum.

    • [x] PIC and FLIP controls; conservative rank-deficient-support handling.

    • [x] Translation, affine reproduction, transfer angular momentum/energy, force-driven evolution, boundary and segregation integration checks.

  • [x] User guides, input example matrix, rendered manual and regression checks.

  • [x] Black formatting, CI formatting/tests/docs/package checks, and Codecov reporting.

  • [x] Manual pypi.yml Trusted Publishing workflow matching the configured pending publisher (no GitHub environment); publication requires explicit dispatch.

  • [x] Hydrostatic equilibrium, translated self-equilibrated stress, and nonlinear manufactured dynamics with analytical references and regression checks.

  • [x] Separate dynamic grid/timestep studies, particle-quadrature studies, frozen exact-state force checks, fixed-cloud remaps, and prescribed affine patches.

  • [x] Present-tense user documentation with measured verification limits.

Acceptance evidence¶

The regression suite includes tests/test_modern_solver.py and tests/test_broader_verification.py. Source-fingerprinted reports in benchmarks/verification.json and benchmarks/broader_verification.json cover complete example runs, standing waves, equilibrium, finite strain, and operator controls. The verification guide explains measured errors and non-monotone levels. Distribution builds and strict HTML documentation checks cover packaging and user instructions. These checks verify implementation; experimental validation and application calibration remain separate tasks.

Deferred implementation backlog¶

  • [ ] Choose a release version, review metadata/README rendering, rehearse on TestPyPI if desired, and verify the first production PyPI upload/install.

  • [ ] Establish coverage thresholds after reviewing the first Codecov baseline.

  • [ ] Control distorted-particle quadrature/cell-crossing force errors; demonstrate spatial convergence beyond the two-particles-per-axis sampling regime.

  • [ ] Well-balanced hydrostatics with quadratic interpolation on general particle clouds.

  • [ ] Higher-order position integration consistent with deformation/stress evolution; isolate timestep accuracy from the number of remaps.

  • [ ] Broader application benchmarks and experimental validation.

  • [ ] Benchmark-driven assessment of GIMP/CPDI or higher-order interpolation, if quadratic boundary/interior accuracy is insufficient.

  • [ ] Locking mitigation: F-bar / mixed pressure formulation, with incompressible benchmarks.

  • [ ] Curved rigid boundaries, contact reactions, friction and separate body fields.

  • [ ] Implicit/quasistatic solver and constitutive consistent tangents.

  • [ ] Finite-strain multiplicative plasticity and calibrated granular constitutive extensions.

  • [ ] Nonlocal granular rheology / size effects, with independent validation data.

  • [ ] Checkpoint/restart including controller and constitutive state.

  • [ ] Conservative particle adaptivity and/or grid refinement.

  • [ ] Three-dimensional mechanics, transport, boundaries, and verification.

  • [ ] Pore-pressure / solid–fluid coupling if required by the intended applications.

  • [ ] Profile and accelerate verified kernels; retain a numerical reference backend.

  • [ ] Experimental validation and application-specific parameter calibration.
